phases.name: Accept happy path plus the public vertical

steps.name: Walking skeleton: set password and land signed in
criteria: A first-admin with a live signed invite opens GET /invites/accept, sees the set-password form, and submits a policy-passing password.
The POST verifies the token, runs check_password_policy, then consumes the invite once and writes the argon2id hash in one tx, establishes a session, and 303-redirects.
She lands on the Northwind workspace dashboard signed in with no separate login step, sees only her own tenant's data, and invites.used_at is set exactly once.
Genuinely RED by MISSING: no /invites/accept route, no show_accept_form or submit_accept handler, no Store consume seam, and no check_password_policy exist yet.
Run cargo xtask check-arch on the new invites_accept.rs; add a LAYER-1e allow-list line for invites_accept ONLY if the run flags it (provisional: no line, mirrors signin).
steps.scenario_name: A first-admin sets her password and lands on her workspace signed in

steps.name: Live invite renders set-password form naming workspace
criteria: Opening a live, unexpired, unused invite link via GET renders a set-password form.
The rendered form names the Northwind workspace for context, confirming the GET resolves the invite's workspace before rendering.
Green-by-inheritance once the walking skeleton's GET handler and template exist.
steps.scenario_name: A live invite renders a set-password form naming the workspace

steps.name: Opening the accept page consumes nothing
criteria: After a GET on a live invite, no password has been set on the first-admin's account.
The invite remains live and unconsumed (used_at still NULL) after the GET; the GET is non-committal and mutates no state.
Proves only the POST consume tx is authoritative, establishing the TOCTOU-safety foundation.
steps.scenario_name: Opening the accept page consumes nothing

steps.name: Invite just inside expiry window is accepted
criteria: An invite one second from expiring (just inside its window) is opened, a valid password is set, and the accept completes.
She is signed in on the Northwind workspace, proving the expiry boundary is inclusive up to expires_at.
Pairs with the just-past-expiry refusal boundary to pin the NFR-1 expiry edge.
steps.scenario_name: An invite opened just inside its expiry window is accepted

steps.name: Expired invite refused without leaking existence
criteria: Opening an invite that expired one day ago returns the standard invite-is-no-longer-valid page.
The page reveals nothing about whether any account or workspace exists and advises asking the instance administrator to re-issue the invite.
This is the canonical refusal arm that scenarios 02-02 through 02-05 assert byte-identity against.
steps.scenario_name: An expired invite is refused without leaking existence

steps.name: Invite just past expiry window is refused
criteria: An invite that expired one second ago (just outside its window) is opened and returns the standard refusal page.
The full response is byte-identical (200 status and full body bytes) to the expired-invite refusal, not merely the same status.
Pairs with the just-inside boundary to pin the expiry edge on the refusal side.
steps.scenario_name: An invite opened just past its expiry window is refused

steps.name: Tampered signature refused identically to expired
criteria: An invite live but with one altered signature character is opened; the HMAC verify fails before any DB hit.
The response is byte-identical (status and full body) to the expired-invite refusal.
The refusal reason appears only in internal tracing keyed on invite_id, never in the observable response.
steps.scenario_name: A tampered signature is refused identically to an expired link

steps.name: Unknown invite id refused identically to others
criteria: Opening an accept link whose id was never issued returns the standard refusal page.
The response is byte-identical (status and full body) to the expired-invite refusal, and nothing reveals whether that id, account, or workspace exists.
A prober cannot distinguish a never-existed id from any other refusal reason.
steps.scenario_name: An unknown invite id is refused identically to every other reason

steps.name: Refusals byte-identical across all four reasons
criteria: Expired, already-used, tampered-signature, and unknown-id links are each opened and all four produce a byte-identical user-visible refusal page (status and full body bytes).
They differ only in internal logging, never in the observable response; collapsing any two arms into divergent responses must re-RED this assertion.
The @property non-enumerability invariant, example-pinned at LAYER 3 (the security crux).
steps.scenario_name: Invalid-link refusals are byte-identical across all four reasons

steps.name: A consumed invite can never be used again
criteria: After a successful accept, re-opening the same invite link returns the standard refusal page.
No new password is set and no session is created on the second use; the guarded UPDATE matches zero rows.
Proves exactly-once single-use at the handler level.
steps.scenario_name: A consumed invite can never be used again

steps.name: Concurrent accepts succeed exactly once
criteria: Two accept submissions for one live invite arrive concurrently; the atomic guarded UPDATE (not a read-then-write) means exactly one submission sets the password and signs in.
The other submission receives the standard refusal page and invites.used_at is recorded as used exactly once.
The @property race oracle for NFR-2, example-pinned at LAYER 3.
steps.scenario_name: Concurrent accepts of one invite succeed exactly once

steps.name: Submission without valid security token refused
criteria: A forged accept POST for a live invite without a valid double-submit token reaches the endpoint and is refused by the shipped csrf_middleware before the handler runs.
No invite is consumed and no password is written.
The CSRF cookie is minted on the GET accept page; the POST mounts under the shipped double-submit layer with no exempt-path entry.
steps.scenario_name: An accept submission without a valid security token is refused

steps.name: No invite signature or password in logs
criteria: After a full successful accept plus a refused hostile-prober cycle, the application logs are examined.
No invite signature value appears in the logs and no submitted password appears in the logs; refusal reasons live in tracing keyed on invite_id only.
The @property no-secret-leakage invariant, example-pinned at LAYER 3.
steps.scenario_name: No invite signature or password ever appears in the logs

steps.name: Link consumed before submit refused by tx guard
criteria: After Priya opens her live invite, the same invite is consumed by another submission before she submits her own valid password on the now-stale page.
She sees the standard refusal page; no second password write occurs and the invite stays used exactly once.
Proves the GET liveness check is advisory only and the consume tx guard re-checks liveness and expiry atomically (TOCTOU closed).
steps.scenario_name: A link consumed between opening the page and submitting is refused by the transaction guard

steps.name: Weak password corrected inline, invite stays live
criteria: Submitting a password below the min-12 strength policy re-renders the form with an inline error explaining the minimum password length.
The policy check runs before the consume tx opens, so the invite stays live and unconsumed and no session is created.
Strands nobody on a dead link: the invite remains re-usable for a valid retry.
steps.scenario_name: A weak password is corrected inline and the invite stays live

steps.name: Mismatched confirmation corrected inline, invite live
criteria: When the confirmation does not match the new password, the form re-renders with an inline error that the passwords do not match.
The invite stays live and unconsumed because the check runs before the consume tx opens.
No consume and no session for a confirmation mismatch.
steps.scenario_name: A mismatched confirmation is corrected inline and the invite stays live

steps.name: Valid retry after error completes the accept
criteria: After being shown an inline password error on a still-live invite, submitting a valid password and confirmation on the same invite completes the accept.
She is signed in on the Northwind workspace and the invite is recorded as used exactly once.
The recoverability proof: an inline error leaves the invite re-usable.
steps.scenario_name: A valid retry on the same invite after an error completes the accept

steps.name: Password exactly at minimum length is accepted
criteria: Submitting a twelve-character password and matching confirmation is accepted by check_password_policy.
Her password is accepted and she is signed in on the Northwind workspace, confirming the policy is at-least-12 (inclusive).
The min-length boundary on the accept side.
steps.scenario_name: A password exactly at the minimum length is accepted
